plan.title: Commitment ask and soft-yes re-ask sound scripted

context.text: Yea I track everything on my whoop app

That's everything I need, here's your plan:
• Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat at 6:30 pm: 75 min lifting at Crunch
• After: a Whoop strain screenshot
Five days after work builds the habit without eating your weekend. What do you think?

transcript.text:
Tracking everything in Whoop makes the proof easy, Yanni. Here's the full plan:

• Day 1 is today: 75 min lifting at Crunch, starting 6:30 pm
• Schedule: Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat at 6:30 pm, 75 min each
• Proof: a screenshot of your Whoop strain after each workout
• Why: five days after work builds the habit without eating your weekend
• Easy alternative: if the strain screen isn't handy, send a photo from the gym

Each workout shapes the next one, so we build from what you actually do. What do you think?
Good. Before we lock it in, I want to hear it from you, Yanni. Are you committing to lifting at Crunch at 6:30 pm, five days a week, starting today?
Let's go, Yanni! 💪 Day 1 is today: 75 minutes of lifting at Crunch, starting at 6:30 pm. Send me that Whoop strain screenshot when you're done.

checks.reason: A plan-presenting text, so up to about 8 lines is allowed; this runs about 8 lines including the closing question.
Uses a plain • list with no markdown, hashtags or filler.
Warm and direct with no emoji row or overfamiliarity.
Uses the Whoop tracking, Crunch, 6:30 pm and five-day schedule the tester already gave.
Day 1 gives what, where, when and how long; the exercise type is only "lifting", which the tester already set.
Two sentences, within the one-to-three limit.
Plain wording with no markdown or filler.
Direct and warm, with no emoji or overfamiliar lines.
Restates only the plan details the tester already agreed to.
Restates the step's place, time and start day without leaving important details open.
Three short sentences, within the limit.
Plain text with a single emoji as punctuation.
Hype line for a real commitment with one emoji, warm and not overfamiliar.
Day 1 details match the agreed plan and the tester's Whoop proof.
Day 1 gives what, where, when and proof: 75 minutes of lifting at Crunch at 6:30 pm, then a Whoop screenshot.

conversation.reason: After "Looks good", ZOH re-shows the full plan as a list and ends with "What do you think?" instead of asking for the commitment, which is the miss the regression case targets.

grade.summary: ZOH's texts are short, warm and grounded in what Yanni said, and the commitment ask after "Ok" is natural with no quoting or pressure. However, after "Looks good" it re-shows the whole plan instead of going straight to the commitment ask, which is the exact regression this case was meant to catch.
